The framing — geopolitical headwinds (Middle East) plus seasonal drag — is consistent with the Q4 data, and the 1H FY27 recovery thesis (normalising Middle East, summer portfolio lapping a weak base) is plausible.

However, KS's own target trajectory tells a clear story: ₹944 (Nov-2024) → ₹645 (Nov-2025) → ₹589 (Feb-2026) → ₹525 (May-2026). That is a consistent downgrade trend across every earnings season, suggesting the recovery keeps slipping one quarter forward. I'd treat the Buy as a valuation-floor argument rather than a growth conviction, and wait for Q1 FY27 data before acting on it.

CLSA|260522.change: No prior CLSA report in the library to compare; Hold initiated at ₹415.
CLSA|260522.view:
CLSA's note is the most bearish in the current pack and the most analytically granular: it pins the EBITDA miss at 16% vs consensus, breaks out gross-margin improvement (255bps YoY — a genuine positive) against EBITDA-margin compression (260bps YoY from operating deleverage and higher A&P), and calls out the summer-portfolio collapse as the decisive drag. At ₹415, CLSA is pricing in very little near-term recovery.

This is the useful counterweight to the consensus-bull stance. The operating-deleverage argument is sound: if revenue grows only weakly or declines, Emami's cost base doesn't flex proportionally, and A&P spending to defend shelf space compounds the margin pressure. I think CLSA's structural concerns are underweighted by the bull houses. ₹415 may be closer to fair value if the growth recovery is another two or three quarters away.

Jeff|260521.view:
Jefferies is technically the most bullish (highest PT at ₹620) but its own language reveals a reluctant bull — the BUY is explicitly "based solely on valuations", not earnings confidence. When an analyst flags that, it is a yellow flag: valuation support works until sentiment turns further negative, and Emami has a history of re-ratings going in the wrong direction.

The flat-EBITDA-for-five-years admission is the most important line in any recent Emami note. Jefferies is essentially arguing: yes, this business hasn't grown earnings in half a decade, but the stock is cheap enough on mean-reversion. That is a reasonable argument in theory, but mean-reversion requires a catalyst — and the Q4 miss doesn't supply one. I'd discount the ₹620 target and focus on whether Q1 FY27 data validates the recovery narrative before treating this as a conviction buy.

MO|260204.change: PT cut ₹675→₹650 (prior Trendlyne entry Nov-2025); Buy maintained.
MO|260204.view:
This is a pre-Q4FY26 note based on Q3FY26 results. MO was cautiously optimistic — steady delivery, positive commentary on growth recovery — but the subsequent Q4 miss makes this view stale. The ₹650 target now sits above even Jefferies' post-miss ₹620, making MO the most optimistic in the current set on an apples-to-apples basis.

MO's view needs to be refreshed post-Q4. The Q3 beat that underpinned this note was followed by a Q4 that missed EBITDA by ~16%. The recovery story MO was banking on did not materialise in Q4. Treat this as an old data point until a post-results update appears.

PL|260204.change: PT cut ₹697→₹571 (prior Trendlyne entry May-2025); Accumulate maintained.
PL|260204.view:
PL's Accumulate from February 2026 is similarly pre-Q4 and based on Q3FY26 results. At ₹571 it is more conservative than MO and Jefferies, and PL's "cautiously optimistic" framing was an honest hedge at the time. PL has historically been more measured on Emami than the bull pack.

Like MO, this view is now stale post-Q4. PL's Accumulate (rather than Buy) has arguably been the more defensible stance given the serial earnings misses. The ₹571 target will likely be revised down once PL refreshes its note for Q4FY26.

Emkay|241110.change: Dated Nov-2024 (over 18 months old); no recent prior to compare.
Emkay|241110.view:
Emkay's Buy at ₹950 from November 2024 is deeply stale — the stock has derated materially since and the company has missed estimates in multiple quarters since that note was written. "Better seasonality and focus on execution" was the thesis in Q2FY25; Emami has delivered neither consistently in the 18 months since.

Disregard this note for current investment decisions. Emkay almost certainly has a refreshed, lower target, but it is not in the library.

AR|241110.change: Dated Nov-2024 (over 18 months old); no recent prior to compare.
AR|241110.view:
Anand Rathi's Buy at ₹900 from November 2024 carries the same staleness problem as Emkay. The TMC trade-channel transition and Bangladesh headwinds AR flagged in Q2FY25 have been followed by further disappointments — the H2 FY25 recovery AR was expecting has not fully played through.

The ₹900 target is not a usable data point in the current context.

Entero Healthcare.summary:
Only **Jefferies** (May 2026) and **Monarch** (Aug 2024) cover Entero in the library — both bullish, no bears. Jefferies is the only current, substantive view: it raised its PT from ₹1,350 to ₹1,500 on the Mar-Q result, maintaining Buy, while flagging a mixed quarter (revenue/EBITDA beat, PAT miss on higher depreciation, finance costs, and elevated minority interest attributed to a one-off). Management guided 23% organic growth and 100bps EBITDA margin expansion in FY27, with growth anchored in consolidating acquisitions and scaling medtech distribution. Monarch's Aug 2024 note (PT ₹1,500, Buy) predates the IPO seasoning period and is now ~22 months stale — its "distribution excellence" framing was directionally right but adds little current signal. The real debate is not bull vs. bear but whether the promised margin expansion is structural or aspirational in a business where gross margins are inherently thin.

My own read: Entero is an interesting consolidation play in Indian pharma distribution — a sector that is deeply fragmented and where scale genuinely creates cost advantages. The IPO (Feb 2024) was richly priced on the promise of being the aggregator, and the story has advanced: acquisitions are in the fold, medtech is a higher-margin vertical that could structurally lift the blended margin over time. That said, I'd be cautious about the PAT quality. "Elevated minority interest" in an acquisition-heavy rollup is rarely a clean one-off — it often reflects the structural reality of buying businesses without full control. Similarly, rising depreciation and finance costs are the inevitable hangover of the inorganic ramp, and the question is whether operating leverage from revenue scaling covers them fast enough. The 23% organic growth guidance is ambitious; I'd watch the quarterly organic vs. inorganic revenue split closely. Jefferies' revised EPS (FY27 cut, FY28 raised) is a reasonable base case but embeds a lot of execution faith. If medtech scaling hits friction or integration costs persist, the FY28 payoff slides further out.

Jeff|260526.change: PT raised ₹1,350→₹1,500; Buy maintained. FY27 EPS cut on higher tax rate and depreciation; FY28 EPS raised on improving margin trajectory.
Jeff|260526.view:
This is the only fresh, data-rich view in the library and it deserves weight. Jefferies' PT raise despite a PAT miss and FY27 EPS cut signals confidence in the medium-term trajectory over near-term noise — that's a defensible call if the margin expansion story holds.

However, I'd push back on the "one-off" characterisation of the minority interest drag. In rollup businesses, minority stakes are often structurally sticky until buy-out, and the cost of financing those buy-outs (via debt or dilution) is itself a risk to the FY28 EPS recovery. The 100bps margin expansion guidance is the key watch — at pharma distribution's thin absolute margins, any execution shortfall is disproportionately visible in PAT.

Monarch|240816.change: Dated Aug 2024; no matching pdfdata entry. Trendlyne shows Monarch had PT ₹1,515 in Jun 2024 and ₹1,500 in Aug 2024 — a marginal TP trim, Buy maintained.
Monarch|240816.view: This note is ~22 months old and essentially stale as a current input. The "distribution excellence" thesis was the IPO-era buy case and the landscape has moved on — acquisitions have closed, medtech has been added, and a full year of listed-company results has accumulated. Monarch's current view on post-acquisition integration and the PAT trajectory is unknown from this library. Treat it as directional background, not active signal.

Eureka Forbes.summary:
Four houses cover Eureka Forbes; two are fresh (Kotak and Nomura, both dated 260520, post-4QFY26 results) and two are stale (ICICI from Nov 2025, East India from Sep 2024). **Kotak** is the most constructive — Buy, PT ₹700 unchanged — absorbing 3–6% EPS cuts on RM inflation via a rolled-forward DCF and flagging management's confidence in WP acceleration. **Nomura** is also Buy but more candid about cost pressure, cutting PT ₹629→₹600 after RM/sales rose ~214 bps q-q in 4Q; it leans on new categories (air purifiers, water softeners) as the incremental growth lever. **ICICI** (Nov 2025, TP ₹685, Buy) lowered its target from ₹735, presumably reflecting moderation in near-term growth — this note predates 4QFY26 and is now ~7 months old. **East India** initiated at Hold in Sep 2024 with a ₹536 PT; at 20+ months old it is essentially irrelevant to current positioning. The real debate is whether RM cost pressure is transient and whether new categories can sustain revenue CAGR once the WP-penetration impulse moderates — Kotak says yes comfortably, Nomura is more watchful, ICICI has yet to update post-results.

My own read: Eureka Forbes owns a genuinely durable franchise — the installed AMC base is a recurring-revenue engine most consumer peers lack, and WP under-penetration in India (sub-20% urban, near-zero rural at meaningful price points) gives the category a long runway. The sell-side's ₹600–700 target band implies the market is pricing in ~12–15% volume CAGR plus steady margin expansion — both plausible but not guaranteed simultaneously. What the bulls are glossing over: RM inflation (steel, polymers) is structural enough to require pricing action, and Eureka's premium positioning limits how aggressively it can pass costs through in a competitive landscape that includes Kent, Havells, and AO Smith all investing in distribution. The new-categories thesis (air purifiers, softeners) is optionally exciting but remains sub-scale today. I'd sit close to Nomura's TP — cautiously constructive — and watch two things: (1) EBITDA margin trajectory over the next two quarters to confirm RM pressure is not worsening; (2) whether services revenue as a share of total crosses 35%+ (the threshold at which AMC recurring cash becomes a meaningful valuation re-rating driver).

Kotak|260520.change: PT unchanged ₹700; Buy maintained. FY2027/28E EPS cut 3–6% on RM inflation; DCF-based fair value rolled forward and held steady.
Kotak|260520.view:
Kotak's steady TP despite EPS cuts tells you the DCF model is absorbing near-term headwinds and discounting the WP penetration story at a long horizon — a defensible call, but it somewhat papers over the cost reality Nomura is more explicit about. The phrase 'management remains confident' recurs, which is a mild yellow flag; management guidance on WP acceleration has historically run ahead of actual delivery in softer macro quarters.

The 12%+ three-year WP volume CAGR is the key metric to anchor to. If that holds through FY27, Kotak's TP is reasonable; if it dips to mid-single digits (which RM-driven consumer fatigue could cause), the DCF quickly erodes. Worth monitoring quarterly rather than anchoring to the annual story.

Nomura|260520.change: PT cut ₹629→₹600; Buy maintained. RM/sales rose ~214 bps q-q to 41.3% in 4QFY26, only partially offset by lower other expenses.
Nomura|260520.view:
Nomura's TP cut is the more intellectually honest call in this earnings cycle — it names the specific RM headwind and adjusts rather than rolling a DCF. Buy at ₹600 is still a reasonable risk/reward if you believe the category remains structurally under-penetrated, but the new-categories lever (air purifiers, water softeners) that Nomura is using to justify 'growth momentum' is still unproven at scale.

The note is useful as a near-term sanity check: if RM/sales doesn't start to ease over the next 1–2 quarters, a further TP trim is plausible and Nomura will likely be the first to move. Watch the quarterly gross-margin line closely.

ICICI|251116.change: No pdfdata match for this note. Prior Trendlyne entry (Dec 2024): TP ₹735, Buy; current note (Nov 2025): TP ₹685, Buy — implies a TP cut of ₹735→₹685 between the two reports, Buy maintained throughout.
ICICI|251116.view: This note is now ~7 months old and pre-dates 4QFY26 results — the RM pressure and TP cuts from Kotak/Nomura have already moved the conversation forward. ICICI's 'under-penetration' thesis is the right structural frame and their gradual TP reduction (₹660 Oct 2024 → ₹735 Dec 2024 → ₹685 Nov 2025) shows they've been modestly recalibrating rather than blindly bullish. That said, the note is too stale to drive a current view. Treat as directionally consistent with the buy case but defer to the fresher Kotak/Nomura reads for near-term guidance.

East|240916.change: Initiation note dated Sep 2024 — no prior East India report in the library or Trendlyne to compare. No more recent note found from this house.
East|240916.view: At 20+ months old and with a ₹536 PT that sits well below the current ₹600–700 consensus cluster, this Hold initiation is effectively a historical artefact. East India's caution at initiation in Sep 2024 was understandable — new entrant to coverage, conservative valuation methodology — but the stock has re-rated materially since then. There is no current signal from this house; ignore for positioning purposes unless a fresh note emerges.

FSN E-commerce Ventures.summary:
Six houses cover Nykaa actively; the consensus leans bullish with one clear Neutral dissent. **Jefferies** (Buy/₹350) and **Nomura** (Buy/₹317) are the most constructive and both raised targets post-Q4FY26 results. **CLSA** (Outperform/₹338) and **Morgan Stanley** (OW, no TP in latest note) round out the bulls. **Kotak** (Add/₹300) is constructively cautious — sees quality but not deep mispricing. **JPMorgan** (Neutral/₹270) is the lone active hold, the lowest TP in the set, and the most explicit on valuation risk. **Geojit** (Accumulate/₹277, Dec 2025) is materially stale — predates the Q4FY26 results. Target spread among fresh notes: ₹270–₹350, with the bull cluster at ₹300–₹350. The real debate is not on operational trajectory — 28% revenue growth, 8.4% EBITDA margin (record), and Fashion EBITDA breakeven are broadly agreed milestones — but on how much of the improvement is already in the price.

My own read: Nykaa is a genuinely differentiated franchise in Indian beauty e-commerce — first-mover brand equity, a sticky own-brands engine (~54% YoY growth) that is both the margin lever and the competitive moat, and a customer repeat-purchase flywheel that is hard to replicate. The Q4FY26 print was legitimately impressive. That said, the sell-side is too uniformly cheerful about Fashion. Fashion EBITDA breakeven in one quarter — achieved partly through marketing efficiency — is not the same as a durable structural turn. Fashion competes directly against Myntra (Flipkart-backed) and Ajio (Reliance-backed), both better-resourced and willing to subsidise growth; one quarter of marketing restraint can flip back negative. The more important watch is **own-brand penetration in Beauty** (the real moat and re-rating driver) and **competitive pressure from Tira** (Reliance's beauty vertical, still early but backed by deep pockets). JPMorgan's Neutral at ₹270 is the most intellectually honest call in the set — it acknowledges the operational improvement while noting current multiples leave limited margin of safety. I'd land closer to Kotak's Add than to Jefferies' aggressive Buy at stiff valuations.

MorganStan|260602.change: PT not disclosed in this note; OW maintained. This is a conference feedback note (India Investment Forum 2026), not a full valuation report — no TP appears in the PDF data.
MorganStan|260602.view: Morgan Stanley's OW is conviction-based but this note adds little new valuation work — it is a management channel check from the firm's own investor forum. The key themes they surfaced: Beauty focused on customer acquisition and purchase frequency; Fashion on curating the right brands and customers. The 'right kind of customers' framing for Fashion is worth noting — it signals management is being selective on Fashion cohorts, the correct strategic call, but one that implicitly limits Fashion's total addressable scale. Weight this note primarily as a sentiment confirmation of MS's existing OW stance rather than a fresh thesis.

CLSA|260522.change: First captured CLSA report in the library — no prior to compare. TP ₹338, Outperform.
CLSA|260522.view: CLSA's Outperform is substantively argued: 28% revenue growth, highest-ever 8.4% EBITDA margin (+195bps YoY), EBITDA 8% above consensus, and own brands up 54% YoY driving margin accretion. The Fashion EBITDA breakeven is correctly flagged as a milestone. One caveat they noted: EBIT missed their estimate due to higher-than-expected depreciation — a structural item to track as Nykaa scales capex in warehousing and tech infrastructure. CLSA's ₹338 TP sits mid-range of the bullish cluster, suggesting they see a clear re-rating path but are not the most aggressive buyer in the group.

JP|260522.change: PT held at ₹270; Neutral maintained — no change vs prior.
JP|260522.view:
JPMorgan is the lone active Neutral in this coverage universe, with a ₹270 target well below the ₹300–₹350 range of the bulls. They acknowledge Q4 EBITDA beat and Fashion's first EBITDA-positive quarter but their Neutral signals the good news is priced in at current levels.

This is arguably the most disciplined call in the set. Nykaa trades at a significant premium to growth peers and JPMorgan's pushback on valuation deserves respect even as the operational trajectory is positive. If the stock re-rated sharply post-Q4 results, JP's ₹270 target implies meaningful downside risk on any execution miss. The key question to watch: at what forward EBITDA multiple does the stock screen, and is the margin expansion trajectory fast enough to justify it? JPMorgan's implicit answer is no, for now.

Kotak|260522.change: First captured Kotak report in the library — no prior to compare. TP ₹300, Add.
Kotak|260522.view:
Kotak's Add is measured optimism. They correctly highlighted BPC contribution margin and EBITDA margin expansion 'despite aggressive investment in customer acquisition' — an important qualifier showing quality of the margin beat — and Fashion EBITDA turning positive. The Add (rather than Buy) rating and ₹300 TP signals they see quality but not sufficient mispricing to go outright bullish.

Kotak is well-regarded for Indian consumer/internet research and their restraint relative to Jefferies is informative. The ₹300 target implies a reasonable medium-term path but not a deeply undervalued situation. This is probably the most balanced house view in the set for someone sizing a position — acknowledges the positives without ignoring valuation.

Jeff|260521.view:
Jefferies is the most bullish voice and the most openly valuation-agnostic — they acknowledge 'stiff valuations' explicitly but argue strong growth supports them. Their insight that Fashion breaking EBITDA even signals management 'cracked the code' is the most structurally important call: if Fashion sustains EBITDA positivity, it removes a drag that has weighed on the investment case for years and significantly changes the group P&L narrative.

I'd stress-test the durability of Fashion breakeven: it was achieved partly through marketing cost discipline (14.3% of sales vs estimates ~15%), which can reverse quickly in a competitive quarter. Jefferies' ₹350 is the most aspirational target in the set — it assumes the margin expansion trajectory continues and the market keeps paying a premium multiple. Worth holding if you believe in the own-brand moat, but the upside-to-downside at ₹350 is narrower than Jefferies implies.

Nomura|260521.view:
Nomura's Buy is grounded in the Q4 margin beat — EBITDA of 8.4% vs their 7.6% estimate, and lower-than-expected marketing costs (14.3% actual vs 15.2% estimate). They are focused on the margin lever story, the right analytical framing: Nykaa's re-rating ultimately depends on sustainable margin expansion, not just GMV momentum.

Nomura's detailed margin disaggregation (RM/sales, marketing costs, EBIT margin line by line) makes this the most technically rigorous note in the set. Their ₹317 TP is more conservative than Jefferies but still above JPMorgan's ₹270. The risk to their Buy: if marketing costs mean-revert higher (they are currently running below historical averages), EBITDA margin could undershoot next quarter and trigger a re-rating in reverse.

Geojit|251211.change: Downgraded Buy→Accumulate; TP ₹277 (Dec 2025). Prior Trendlyne entry (May 2024): Buy at ₹186. No more recent Geojit report in the library — this note is ~6 months old as of Jun 2026.
Geojit|251211.view: Geojit's Dec 2025 Accumulate is materially stale — it predates the Q4FY26 results that drove the bullish re-rating from peers, and it predates Fashion's first EBITDA-positive print. Their ₹277 TP now sits below even JPMorgan's Neutral ₹270 target and well below the ₹300–₹350 range of updated notes. The downgrade from Buy in May 2024 (at ₹186) to Accumulate in Dec 2025 (at ₹277) likely reflected valuation stretch at that point in time. Discount this view heavily; it is not representative of the post-Q4FY26 picture.

Finolex Cables.summary:
Jefferies (Jun 2026, Buy ₹1,200) is the sole fresh and outright bull in the coverage — raising its PT from ₹1,000 to ₹1,200 after a strong Mar-Q beat and citing the stock still trading at ~19x FY27 PE, in-line with its 10-year historical average despite a +30% YTD run. The remaining three houses are materially staler: Geojit downgraded to Accumulate (Mar 2026, PT ₹1,008), Anand Rathi maintained Buy but cut PT to ₹975 (Nov 2025), and Sharekhan's Buy at ₹1,650 (Aug 2024) is nearly two years old and effectively vestigial. The real tension is between Jefferies' valuation-anchored bull case and the Geojit/AR cluster whose targets sit at or below current market price — making them inadvertent Sell signals rather than constructive views. No broker carries a formal Sell; the bear case is expressed purely through stale or below-CMP price targets.

My own read: Finolex is a credible franchise — among the stronger brands in Indian wires and cables, benefiting from housing/infra tailwinds and disciplined price-hike pass-through (~20% in FY26 to offset copper). The +30% YTD rally looks earnings-driven rather than re-rating-driven if Jefferies' 21x FY27 PE is accurate, and that multiple being in-line with the historical mean is a fair base case. That said, the concentration risk is real: ~85% of revenue is in electrical cables, making the stock highly sensitive to copper price trajectory and housing-cycle duration. The persistent FMEG drag (fans, switches) has been improving toward positive EBIT but remains a value detractor until it scales. I'd monitor the OFC opportunity closely — optical fibre cable is a genuine growth vector if government broadband rollout accelerates, but it's early. On balance, Jefferies is the only view worth running with today; the rest of the coverage needs refreshing before drawing conclusions.

Jeff|260601.view:
The freshest and most substantive note in the coverage. The valuation argument holds up — 21x/18x FY27/28e PE at or below the 10-year average, while the operational picture is improving (cable volumes healthy across Auto, Flexible, Power; ~20% cumulative price hikes in FY26 passing copper costs through; FMEG turning positive EBIT). The ₹1,200 PT implies a meaningful premium to the Geojit/AR cluster and is the only call that currently offers real upside if correct.

The risks Jefferies underplays: copper is the central variable — Finolex is a price-taker on input costs, and any reversal of the pass-through ability (competitive pressure from newer entrants like Polycab, KEI) would quickly compress margins. The OFC bet is worth watching but modest in the near term. I'd track the Q1 FY27 volume numbers and whether FY27 EPS delivery stays on track; if so, the ₹1,200 target is reasonable.

Geojit|260318.change: Downgraded Buy→Accumulate; PT nudged ₹988 (Oct 2025)→₹1,008 (Mar 2026). No pdfdata entry; derived from trendlyne.
Geojit|260318.view:
A downgrade paired with a token PT raise is a textbook conviction-trimming move — Geojit is essentially saying the easy money has been made. With a PT of ₹1,008 in March 2026 and the stock subsequently running +30% YTD (per Jefferies' June note), this Accumulate has almost certainly become a de-facto Sell relative to CMP. The note is now three months old and likely below the current price.

Geojit's PT history tells a story of persistent conservatism: ₹1,019 (Mar 2024) → ₹1,354 (Dec 2024, Accumulate) → ₹988 (Oct 2025, Buy on the dip) → ₹1,008 (Mar 2026, back to Accumulate as it rallied). They've oscillated between Buy and Accumulate across the cycle without conviction. I'd treat the Geojit view as a cautious valuation cap rather than a directional call, and note it needs updating before any weight can be placed on it.

AR|251124.change: PT cut ₹1,031→₹975; Buy maintained. Note dated Nov 2025 — over 6 months old.
AR|251124.view:
Anand Rathi has been persistently bullish through a steep PT compression cycle: from ₹1,577 (Nov 2024) to ₹1,031 (Aug 2025) to ₹975 (Nov 2025). The 'mixed performance, steady H2 recovery' thesis from November appears to have partially played out — Jefferies' Mar-Q note flags a strong quarter. But at ₹975, AR's PT is well below Jefferies' ₹1,200, and almost certainly below CMP given the +30% YTD move.

This note is effectively stale and its PT inadvertently signals downside. The persistent Buy rating despite cut-upon-cut-upon-cut PTs suggests AR may be anchoring to an outdated earnings model. I'd assign low weight until AR refreshes with post-Mar-Q numbers.

Sharekhan|240819.change: PT cut ₹1,800→₹1,650; Buy maintained. Note dated Aug 2024 — nearly 2 years old.
Sharekhan|240819.view: Entirely stale — this predates the full copper-volatility-driven margin compression, the FY25 earnings cuts, and the subsequent recovery. Sharekhan has not published a follow-up visible in the data. The ₹1,650 PT is above even Jefferies' current bull case of ₹1,200, reflecting market conditions from a different phase of the cycle entirely. Ignore for current thesis purposes; check whether Sharekhan still actively covers the stock.

Finolex Industries.summary:
The four houses covering Finolex Industries post-Q4FY26 split into two clear camps. **Jefferies** (Buy, PT ₹220, raised from ₹195) and **Anand Rathi** (Buy, PT ₹240) are constructive — both see favourable risk/reward after a margin beat in Q4 (OPM ~25% vs ~14.6% the prior year), with Jefferies framing it as an Agri/rural and plumbing-mix-upgrade play at a ~19x FY27E multiple in line with the 10-year historical average. **Prabhudas Lilladhar** downgraded to Accumulate (PT ₹207, cut from ₹228), judging the margin beat as partly inventory-driven and volumes too subdued to warrant a Buy. **BOB Capital** holds its Hold/₹190 from February — effectively the bear anchor after cutting from Buy in late 2025 — and has not moved despite the Q4 beat. **IDBI Capital**'s Hold predates the Q4 results by nearly 10 months and is stale. The real debate is whether the ~25% Q4 OPM reflects a durable cost reset or a one-quarter inventory/spread gain, and whether FY27 volumes recover after FY26's 4% decline.

My own read: Finolex is fundamentally a commodity processor — it buys PVC resin (imported, USD-priced) and converts it to pipes. When resin prices ease or inventory spreads are favourable, OPM spikes; when they normalise, OPM collapses. The Q4 beat looks at least partly mechanical in that context, which is what PL and BOB are pricing in. The agri pipe skew (~65% of volume mix) makes the business weather-dependent and cyclical around rural spend; the pivot toward plumbing/fittings (~37% now, targeting ~50% over five years) is the right strategy but is a multi-year execution story facing better-capitalised incumbents — Astral Poly, Supreme Industries, Prince Pipes. At ~19x FY27E the stock is at its long-run mean: fair, but not cheap enough to provide a buffer if volumes disappoint again. I would want to see sustained FY27 volume growth — not just another margin print — and preferably two consecutive strong plumbing-segment quarters before adding conviction. For now I would sit roughly in line with PL's Accumulate stance: fine to hold, but the asymmetry for a fresh Buy is not yet compelling.

BOB|260529.change: Hold maintained at ₹190; unchanged vs the Feb 2026 prior note (also Hold/₹190). BOB cut from Buy (PT ₹240) to Hold (PT ₹190) in its February 2026 note — the current update makes no adjustment despite the Q4 margin beat.
BOB|260529.view:
BOB Capital has traced a full disappointment arc on this stock: Buy at ₹265 (May 2025) → Buy at ₹240 (Nov 2025) → Hold at ₹190 (Feb 2026) → Hold at ₹190 today. The flat update after a strong Q4 print speaks volumes; they are not persuaded the beat changes the volume trajectory. At ₹190 BOB's target sits well below where Jefferies and Anand Rathi are anchored, making it the effective bear anchor in this coverage set.

I give this view meaningful weight. BOB has been consistently cautious as actual volume prints disappointed, and the Q4 margin beat being inventory-spread-related rather than volume-driven does not obviously change their thesis. The Hold/₹190 probably requires a genuine FY27 volume rebound to move — until that data exists, the bear case has not been invalidated.

Jeff|260528.view:
Jefferies makes a disciplined valuation argument: after a +11% five-day move the stock still trades at ~19x FY27E, in line with the historical average, so the re-rating has not yet run ahead of itself. The Agri/rural framing and the plumbing mix-shift thesis (targeting ~50% plumbing from ~37% today) are both structurally sound angles.

That said, the PT raise to ₹220 rests partly on a Q4 margin beat that was at least partly driven by inventory gains rather than pure volume/mix improvement. Jefferies is right that the risk/reward is reasonable if FY27 volumes recover, but the Buy rating requires that assumption to materialise — with FY26 volumes already down 4%, any weather or demand disruption in FY27 would stress the model. The ₹220 target is defensible as a base case; the conviction would deepen if Q1FY27 volumes come in positive.

PL|260528.change: Downgraded to Accumulate (headline states 'Downgrade to ACCUMULATE'); PT cut to ₹207 from ₹228 (last captured note, Aug 2025). The trendlyne history does not show an intermediate Buy rating, but the 'downgrade' language implies PL had moved above Accumulate at some point not captured in the library.
PL|260528.view:
PL's downgrade is arguably the most analytically rigorous call in this set post-Q4. They acknowledge the margin beat but correctly identify that subdued volumes mean the earnings quality is partially illusory — inventory-spread gains inflate OPM in a way that does not compound. The PT cut to ₹207 signals they are not chasing the recent re-rating.

The Accumulate label at ₹207 (below current trading levels given the +11% move) is essentially saying 'do not add at these prices.' I find this the most disciplined read in the coverage: the plumbing pivot is real but multi-year, the agri volume base is weather-sensitive, and after a strong quarter on margin the stock is no longer cheap enough to absorb the volume risk. PL's caution is the right counterweight to Jefferies and AR's bullishness.

AR|260527.change: Buy maintained at PT ₹240 ('Maintain BUY' per headline). No prior Anand Rathi report in the library or trendlyne history to compare TP movement.
AR|260527.view:
Anand Rathi's Buy/₹240 is the most optimistic target in the set, implying roughly a 9% premium to Jefferies' ₹220 and ~20% above PL/BOB. Without a prior AR report in the library I cannot see what earnings or valuation assumptions drive ₹240 — whether it embeds a faster volume recovery, a higher margin assumption, or a target multiple re-rating.

At face value ₹240 requires either a sustained volume rebound that the FY26 track record does not yet support, or a conviction that the plumbing mix shift is happening faster than other houses model. I would treat AR's view as the bull case but would want to see the model before adding weight to it. The 'Maintain BUY' language suggests they have held this view through the volume weakness — which either reflects patience or anchoring bias; without prior data it is hard to distinguish.

IDBI|250806.change: Downgraded from Buy (PT ₹234, Feb 2025) to Hold (PT ₹207, Aug 2025). Note is approximately 10 months old and predates Q4FY26 results; no update captured since.
IDBI|250806.view:
This note is stale — it was written after Q1FY26 results and predates the Q4FY26 margin beat and the subsequent re-rating. The downgrade at the time reflected weak Q1 volumes and monsoon-driven demand uncertainty, which were legitimate concerns. IDBI's ₹207 target has since been overtaken by the PL Accumulate at the same level and Jefferies' Buy at ₹220.

Given the age, I would place minimal weight on this view for current positioning. IDBI may have updated since (August 2025 is their last trendlyne capture in the dataset) and the thesis has likely evolved with Q2–Q4 prints. The downgrade history is a useful reminder that this stock has a record of disappointing volume bears, but the specific ₹207 Hold is not actionable as a current signal.

Fortis Healthcare.summary:
Four of the six houses are bullish — **JPMorgan** (OW, PT ₹1,120), **Jefferies** (Buy, PT ₹1,125), **Prabhudas Lilladhar** (Buy, PT ₹1,050), and **Geojit** (Buy, PT ₹1,030) — while **Nomura** (Neutral, PT ₹990) and **ICICI** (Hold, PT ₹970) are cautious. The bull cluster anchors around ₹1,050–1,125, with the two neutrals sitting ₹100–150 below. JP trimmed its PT modestly to ₹1,120 from ₹1,150 even after a solid 4QFY26 beat, suggesting controlled optimism. The real debate is margin delivery: management has guided 15%+ hospital revenue growth and 100bps EBITDA margin improvement for FY27, targeting 25% hospital margins by FY28. Nomura is the dissenting voice — it flagged a 3% EBITDA miss and a 109bp margin miss in 4Q despite the revenue beat, noting that a lower effective tax rate (not operations) flattered the headline PAT number. ICICI is the most structurally cautious on valuation, with a stale November 2025 note that predates the 4QFY26 prints.

My own read: Fortis is the most credible #2 hospital platform in India — IHH's ownership provides capital depth and international clinical benchmarking that standalone chains can't match. The brownfield-led expansion is the right model: lower cost, faster ramp, and it preserves ROCE. But I'd be closer to Nomura's PT than Jefferies' — the 25% margin target by FY28 requires consistent quarterly execution, and Fortis has historically guided optimistically and delivered with a lag. The diagnostic segment (SRL) is an under-discussed drag: it faces structural margin compression in an intensely competitive market against Lal Path Labs and Metropolis, and the 11% revenue growth Jefferies highlighted is better than feared but the margin trajectory there is weaker. The two things to watch most: (1) quarter-by-quarter hospital EBITDA margin (each print is a direct scorecard on the FY27 guide), and (2) whether the ~400 FY27 brownfield beds ramp occupancy without pulling the blended margin down in the interim.

JP|260526.view:
JPMorgan is the most up-to-date bull in this set (note dated 26 May 2026). The PT trim is modest and the OW stance is firm — it reads as a minor model refresh after 4QFY26 rather than a change of view. JP's core thesis is the compounding nature of Fortis's growth and management's credible path to 25% hospital margins by FY28.

What I'd push back on: JP is largely crediting management guidance at face value. Nomura's concurrent note on the same quarter flags an EBITDA margin miss that JP's framing as a 'beat' doesn't fully square with. Still, the OW is defensible — Fortis's consistency as an organic growth compounder is real — and the slight PT reduction is actually a healthy signal of discipline.

Jeff|260525.view:
Jefferies holds the highest PT in the set and is the most constructive. Its differentiated contribution is the diagnostics angle: 11% revenue growth in 4Q is described as a multi-year high, and the 100bps margin improvement guide for diagnostics alongside the 150bps hospital guide is taken as actionable rather than aspirational.

I'd be somewhat more sceptical: Jefferies is stacking two margin expansion assumptions (hospitals and diagnostics) in a quarter where EBITDA already missed estimates. The ₹1,125 PT implies the market will rerate upward on margin delivery that isn't yet visible in the numbers. The Buy is reasonable as a 12-month call given the structural demand story, but I'd want to see one or two clean margin prints before trusting the full target.

Nomura|260523.view:
The most rigorous recent note in the set. Nomura's flag — EBITDA missing by 3% and margin by 109bp in a quarter the bulls describe as a 'beat' — is the most useful piece of analysis here. The PAT 'beat' is explicitly attributed to a lower effective tax rate, not operational outperformance. There was also an exceptional impairment loss on an associate that distorts the clean read.

I think Nomura's hesitation is the correct instinct. A revenue beat + EBITDA miss pattern in hospital chains often signals that volume growth is coming at the cost of case-mix dilution or cost absorption from new beds. The ₹990 PT is conservatively grounded and the most defensible if margin expansion stalls. This is the note I'd weight most heavily when triangulating the investment case.

PL|260217.change: PT raised ₹1,000→₹1,050 (vs Aug 2025 trendlyne entry); Buy maintained.
PL|260217.view:
This is a Q3FY26 result note from February 2026 — now 4+ months old and predating the 4QFY26 prints. PL raised its PT citing broad-based growth across hospital and diagnostics segments. The directional read was correct at the time, but the subsequent quarter showed EBITDA pressure that this note couldn't anticipate.

I'd treat this as background context rather than an active conviction signal. PL's consistent Buy across multiple quarters (PT progression ₹785→₹1,000→₹1,050) reflects the stock's re-rating trajectory and the underlying business momentum, but the specific thesis here is stale.

Geojit|251222.change: Upgraded to Buy with PT ₹1,030 (Dec 2025); no prior Geojit entry in the library to compare.
Geojit|251222.view:
An upgrade in December 2025, now roughly 6 months old with no subsequent refresh evident. The ₹1,030 PT is the lowest among the bulls and suggests a cautious upgrade — Geojit appears to have turned constructive on IHH's backing and the improving execution trend, but with less upside conviction than JP or Jefferies.

The note is effectively stale at this point. With the 4QFY26 results in and most houses refreshing, Geojit's December view is best treated as supportive background colour rather than a current active call.

ICICI|251113.change: Dated Nov 2025; prior ICICI entry in trendlyne is from Aug 2023 — too old for a meaningful delta. Hold at PT ₹970.
ICICI|251113.view:
The most cautious and the most stale note in the set — now 7 months old and the only Hold. ICICI's thesis was that execution and network expansion support growth, but the valuation didn't justify Buy. The PT of ₹970 is the lowest in the set, implying almost no upside from the likely prevailing price when written.

The fundamental thesis has broadly held up since November 2025 — Fortis has continued to deliver 19% hospital revenue growth — but the valuation argument may have been overtaken by earnings growth. Worth checking whether ICICI has refreshed post 4QFY26; if not, this Hold should be read as an unupdated view rather than an active negative call.

Fusion Finance.summary:
Four houses cover Fusion Finance but their vintage and conviction differ sharply. **CLSA** (May 2026, HOLD ₹205) is the freshest and most credible read: it acknowledges the first AUM growth in six quarters (+8% QoQ in 4QFY26) and a PAT beat from lower provisions and tax writebacks, but flags that PPOP has been rangebound for five consecutive quarters and NII moderated 4% QoQ despite AUM growth — so operating leverage is not yet materialising. **ICICI** (Nov 2025, Buy ₹225) executed a sharp reversal after being Sell at ₹160 in Feb-2025, now the most bullish live view; its TP sits above CLSA's fresh ₹205 HOLD, a tension worth noting. **MO** (May 2025, Neutral ₹170) is the most conservative live TP and has stayed cautious through the recovery phase — roughly 12 months stale now. **Emkay** (Sep 2024, Sell ₹260) is effectively dormant — nearly 21 months old; the management-change and going-concern concerns it flagged were valid at the trough but the situation has evolved. The real debate is whether 4QFY26 marks the genuine inflection or merely a one-quarter relief from lower provisioning.

My own read: Fusion is a textbook MFI cycle recovery story, but the quality of the recovery matters. The CLSA note's detail is sobering: NII falling QoQ even as AUM grows signals yield compression or a mix shift toward lower-rate borrowers — not the kind of NIM expansion you want to see at the start of a new growth cycle. Five quarters of flat PPOP tells you cost efficiencies and revenue growth are largely offsetting each other, not compounding. ICICI's Buy at ₹225 captures directional improvement but was written before the 4QFY26 print that revealed this NII headwind; I'd treat it as partially stale. MO's ₹170 Neutral may now understate fair value if the AUM trough is genuinely behind us, but the gap between ₹170 and ₹225 essentially captures the range of outcomes. The two things I'd watch most: (1) whether NII returns to sequential growth in 1QFY27 — AUM growing while NII shrinks is unsustainable and will cap RoA recovery; and (2) net credit cost trajectory — provisional tailwind was a big driver of the 4QFY26 PAT beat, and the stress pool resolution needs to be genuine, not just write-offs.

CLSA|260518.view:
The freshest note in the set and the most granular. CLSA's HOLD at ₹205 is defensible: it credits the AUM growth inflection and PAT beat but refuses to extrapolate — the observation that PPOP has been 'rangebound for five quarters' is the key restraint. That's not a recovery story yet; it's a stabilisation story.

The NII-down-4%-QoQ-while-AUM-up-8% signal is the detail I'd stress-test most. If yield compression is structural (borrower mix, competitive pressure on rates, or MCLR-linked liabilities catching up), PPOP will stay rangebound even as volumes recover. CLSA's cautious hold is the right anchor for now; I'd need two quarters of NII expansion before upgrading conviction.

ICICI|251107.change: Upgraded from Sell (PT ₹160, Feb-2025) to Buy; PT raised to ₹225.
ICICI|251107.view:
ICICI's swing from ₹160 Sell to ₹225 Buy in nine months captures the violence of the MFI sentiment cycle. The upgrade in Nov 2025 likely reflected early collection improvement data and a stabilising stress pool — and directionally it was correct, as 4QFY26 did show the first AUM growth in six quarters.

However, at roughly 7 months old, the Buy at ₹225 predates the 4QFY26 print that showed NII moderation. CLSA's contemporaneous ₹205 HOLD, written with full sight of the quarter, sits below ICICI's target — which suggests the market and fresher analysts are less excited. ICICI's track record on this stock (₹800 Buy in FY23 → ₹160 Sell → ₹225 Buy) reflects that it has been reactive rather than anticipatory. I'd treat the Buy as a directional call that is roughly right but may be TPing ahead of where the fundamentals currently sit.

MO|250526.change: PT trimmed ₹175→₹170 (vs Feb-2025 Neutral); Neutral maintained.
MO|250526.view:
MO has held Neutral through the entire recovery phase and is the most conservative live view on price (₹170 vs CLSA ₹205, ICICI ₹225). The marginal PT trim to ₹170 in May 2025 reflects persistent scepticism — MO had flagged going-concern uncertainty as recently as Nov 2024. That disciplined caution is worth respecting even if ₹170 now looks like an underestimate post-4QFY26.

At 12+ months old, MO's note predates the AUM growth inflection and the latest provisioning data. Their Neutral may be due for revision if 1QFY27 continues the sequential improvement trend. Still, MO being the lowest TP in the pack is a useful counterweight to ICICI's optimism — the gap between ₹170 and ₹225 essentially defines the bull/base spread of outcomes.

Emkay|240923.change: Dated Sep-2024; no prior Emkay note in the library to compare.
Emkay|240923.view:
Emkay's Sep-2024 Sell at ₹260 is nearly 21 months old and should be treated as historical context rather than a live signal. The concerns it raised — higher LLP guidance and management change — were valid at the trough of the cycle. The going-concern flag from auditors (noted in MO's Nov-2024 report) came shortly after, confirming the severity of the stress at that point.

Since then, management has had over a year to stabilise operations, and 4QFY26 suggests the worst of the credit cycle may be past. The Sell at ₹260 is also paradoxically above CLSA's current HOLD TP of ₹205 — meaning the stock may have re-rated down since Emkay wrote. I'd discard this as a pricing input entirely and keep it only as a reminder of how deep the trough was.

GAIL India.summary:
Five brokers published fresh May-2026 notes, all bullish: **Kotak** upgraded to ADD (PT ₹175, "worst behind"), **Nomura** raised PT ₹185→195 (BUY), **CLSA** held steady at ₹185 (OP), **JPMorgan** raised ₹190→200 (OW), and **Jefferies** cut ₹185→180 (BUY, the lone fresh PT reduction). **BOB Capital Markets** (SELL ₹147, May 2026) is the sole bear, downgraded from HOLD in February on persistent LNG-price volatility. **Motilal Oswal** (BUY ₹220, Nov 2025) and **Prabhudas Lilladhar** (HOLD ₹180, Jul 2025) are both stale and should be treated as historical reference only. The central debate is whether the Middle East–driven earnings one-offs are genuinely transient or signal a structurally impaired gas marketing segment. CLSA's "all-round beat" framing (stripping all one-offs) diverges sharply from Jefferies' and Kotak's "weak quarter" read — the gap is methodological rather than a disagreement on business fundamentals. At CMP ~₹161, the fresh bull cluster implies 9–24% upside (₹175–200); BOB's ₹147 is ~9% downside. JPMorgan is the most structurally confident, Jefferies the most cautious bull.

My own read: GAIL's pipeline transmission moat is genuine — 12,000+ km of trunk gas infrastructure is not replicated — but the stock is an event-driven, not a compounding, story. Two binary catalysts determine whether this is a 15–20% re-rating or dead money: (1) the **PNGRB tariff revision**, delayed for years and capable of materially re-rating transmission earnings if finally issued; and (2) **Middle East conflict resolution**, which determines how fast gas marketing margins recover. Without both, the FY27 earnings base is fragile. I would discount MO's ₹220 as a live target — it predates the FY26 deterioration — and would be more cautious than the May-2026 bull cluster until the tariff order is actually gazetted. The petrochemicals segment (Pata complex) is a low-quality contributor: cyclical, capital-heavy, no competitive moat. Jefferies' FY27/28 EPS upgrades driven by a depreciation-rate cut rather than EBITDA improvement is a yellow flag — flatters earnings without improving cash generation. BOB's ₹147 is too punitive if you value the transmission business on an infrastructure basis, but their caution on marketing-margin volatility is structurally sound. The two things to watch most: tariff order timeline and any ceasefire or LNG-flow restoration news from the Middle East.

Kotak|260525.change: Kotak explicitly upgraded to ADD in this report (report text: "upgrade to ADD"); PT ₹175. No prior Kotak GAIL note in the library — pdfdata prevTP and prevCall are both null — so a numerical prior PT cannot be stated.
Kotak|260525.view:
Kotak's "worst behind; disruption a blessing" thesis is the boldest reframe in the cohort: the Middle East disruption is perversely supportive for GAIL's pipeline volumes long-term, as costly LNG imports incentivise domestic pipeline sourcing. The 4Q weakness (EBITDA −43% YoY, 34% miss) is treated as a cyclical trough. ADD at ₹175 implies only ~9% upside to CMP, so even the upgraded Kotak view is measured, not high-conviction.

The "blessing" argument is intriguing but contingent on India's gas demand routing more through GAIL's pipelines rather than LNG terminals — plausible but not guaranteed. Kotak's upgrade is still at the cautious end of the bull cluster relative to JPMorgan and Nomura. Worth monitoring whether Q1FY27 data confirms the trough thesis or undermines it.

Nomura|260525.view:
Nomura's "resilient earnings despite the war" framing is the most sanguine reading of 4QFY26. Their ₹195 target reflects confidence that once the INR6.7bn fertiliser subsidy provision (accounting, not operational) is stripped, the underlying business held up acceptably. The qualifier is that their own adjusted EBITDA still came in 27% below their estimate — "resilient" is therefore generous.

Nomura's provision-adjusted methodology is analytically defensible, and the PT raise to ₹195 is directionally sound if the conflict resolves within FY27. The risk is that 1Q reconfirms pressure even on an adjusted basis, in which case the ₹195 target looks premature. Among the fresh bulls, Nomura sits between CLSA's unchanged ₹185 and JPMorgan's ₹200 — a reasonable middle ground.

CLSA|260524.view:
CLSA's "all-round beat" headline is the starkest divergence in the May-2026 cohort: where Kotak and Jefferies flagged a miss, CLSA's one-off-adjusted read finds Ebit beat across every segment. Their methodology strips the fertiliser subsidy provision and other one-offs to reveal the operational picture, which they read as intact.

I give CLSA's analytical framework more credit than the headline suggests. If you are valuing GAIL on normalised transmission plus petrochemical Ebit, the 4Q was actually decent. The unchanged ₹185 target — same as Jefferies' cut-to price — implies CLSA is the most conservatively priced of the non-PT-cut bulls, and therefore potentially the most actionable if the operational beat is confirmed next quarter.

JP|260524.view:
JPMorgan holds the highest fresh target (₹200) and is the most structurally confident. Their framing — "managing volumes until the Strait reopens" — treats the disruption as a pure timing issue, not structural impairment, and raises the PT despite explicitly acknowledging 1Q downside risk. That combination signals high conviction in the normalisation thesis.

The ₹200 OW is credible if the Strait situation resolves within two to three quarters. It is, however, a binary geopolitical bet: if the conflict extends into FY28, the PT is at material risk. I would weight JPMorgan's view heavily as a scenario anchor if you are bullish on conflict resolution, but it is the most exposed of the bull targets to a prolonged disruption.

Jeff|260524.view:
Jefferies is the most cautious bull — the only one to cut its PT — and is also the most transparent about a nuance worth flagging: FY27/28 EBITDA is cut 8% for FY27, yet EPS is raised 20%/29% on a sharp depreciation-rate reduction from asset life extensions. This means the earnings upgrade is accounting-driven, not operational — cash generation and underlying business quality are not improving at the same rate as reported EPS.

The ₹180 maintained Buy implies the stock is at fair value with upside only on normalisation. I find Jefferies' note the most analytically honest of the bulls. The depreciation revision is a legitimate accounting change but flatters earnings in a way that could mislead if taken at face value. A useful counterweight to the more sanguine Nomura and JPMorgan targets.

BOB|260522.change: Downgraded from HOLD (PT ₹153, Feb 2026) to SELL (PT ₹147, May 2026); per trendlyne.
BOB|260522.view:
BOB Capital Markets is the lone bear and the view most worth stress-testing. Their concern — persistent LNG-price volatility structurally impairing gas marketing margins — is not merely a reaction to one weak quarter; it follows three consecutive disappointing prints. The SELL at ₹147 implies ~9% downside from CMP ~₹161.

I think ₹147 is too punitive if the transmission business is valued on a stable infrastructure basis — pipeline assets do not lose intrinsic value with LNG price swings. But BOB is structurally right that gas marketing earnings are genuinely volatile and that the petrochemicals segment amplifies rather than cushions that risk. Use BOB's target as a downside scenario if both the PNGRB tariff hike and Middle East normalisation are delayed past FY27.

MO|251130.change: PT raised ₹205→220; Buy maintained (per trendlyne, Nov 2025). This report predates the Middle East disruption's full FY26 earnings impact.
MO|251130.view:
Motilal Oswal's ₹220 is the highest target in the peer set but is dated November 2025 — before Q3/Q4FY26 earnings weakness was fully reflected. Their thesis centred on the PNGRB gas tariff hike as the structural re-rating catalyst, which remains valid in principle but unresolved in practice.

Treat ₹220 as a scenario upside — valid if both the tariff order arrives and the Middle East normalises — not a base-case reference. The gap between MO's ₹220 and the fresh May-2026 bull cluster (₹175–200) captures the earnings deterioration that has occurred since November. A fresh MO note would almost certainly revise this target down.

PL|250729.change: PT cut ₹191→180; Hold maintained (per trendlyne, Jul 2025). Dated ~11 months ago; predates the 2HFY26 gas-marketing weakness.
PL|250729.view:
Prabhudas Lilladhar's HOLD at ₹180 is only marginally above CMP ~₹161 and was published nearly a year ago, before the Middle East disruption materially hit Q2–Q4FY26 margins. The PT cut from ₹191 reflected caution after an in-line but uninspiring Q1FY26 result.

The HOLD stance has broadly been validated by events — the stock has not re-rated despite multiple bull upgrades elsewhere — but the note itself is too stale to inform current positioning. A fresh PL view would likely maintain the cautious framing given the subsequent earnings deterioration; the ₹180 TP effectively functions as a near-term ceiling at current prices.

Grasim Industries.summary:
All five covering houses are bullish — **MorganStanley** (OW, ₹3,900), **Motilal Oswal** (Buy, ₹3,700), **Jefferies** (Buy, ₹3,600), **JPMorgan** (OW, ₹3,460), and **Kotak** (ADD, ₹3,335) — with targets spanning a ₹565 range. The most notable recent move is **Kotak upgrading to ADD** and raising its PT from ₹3,000 to ₹3,335, reflecting the Street's historically most cautious voice moving off the fence after a strong Q4FY26 print. JPMorgan raised PT ₹3,180→₹3,460 while explicitly flagging the elevated holdco discount. Jefferies lifted PT ₹3,440→₹3,600 and sees B2B ecommerce (Pivot) turning profitable by FY27 exit. MorganStanley holds the highest target at ₹3,900, unchanged after a post-India Investment Forum 2026 management interaction. MO's Buy at ₹3,700 is the most dated note (Feb 2026), predating Q4 results. The real debate sits in two places: (1) the pace of paints EBITDA breakeven — all houses acknowledge 19% QoQ revenue growth and narrowing losses but differ on when it becomes a net positive, with FY27 the consensus glide path; and (2) the holdco discount, which JP flags remains structurally wide even as standalone performance has been strong.

**My own read:** Grasim is a conglomerate layering a paint startup onto a core VSF/Chemicals business and large listed stakes in UltraTech and Aditya Birla Capital — a structure that almost guarantees a persistent holdco discount. The sell-side is collectively bullish because parts-sum exceeds the price, but that math has been true for years and the discount has not closed. The paint venture is the crux: the company has deployed ₹100bn+ in a five-player market (Asian Paints, Berger, Indigo, Akzo, Birla Opus) where brand and distribution density are the moat, not just capacity. The FY27 breakeven trajectory is plausible but optimistic if competitive intensity sustains — conference readouts from IIF 2026 reinforce the official narrative, but I'd want to stress-test whether Birla Opus is gaining sustainable share or buying it via promotions. The VSF tailwind (low pulp prices, mix improvement) is real but cyclical; margins at peak pulp will look very different. Two things to watch: (a) Birla Opus quarterly revenue and loss trajectory in H1FY27 vs company guidance; (b) whether the holdco discount compresses as UltraTech continues to re-rate.

MorganStan|260603.change: PT unchanged at ₹3,900; OW maintained. This is a post-India Investment Forum 2026 management-feedback note (hosted CFO Hemant Kadel and IR Head Ankit Panchmatia), not a full research or earnings update.
MorganStan|260603.view:
Morgan Stanley holds the Street's highest target at ₹3,900 (~31% upside from CMP ₹2,971 at the time), and this conference note keeps the bull thesis in place without freshly stress-testing it. As a readout of management messaging rather than an independent model update, it carries less analytical weight than a post-results note — it signals conviction maintenance rather than a new catalyst.

I'd treat the IIF interaction as a confidence signal, not new information. The ₹3,900 target is premised on meaningful holdco discount compression as the paint venture matures and Pivot scales — a sequence that is directionally plausible but whose timing is hard to pin down. MorganStanley's persistently high target makes it useful as the ceiling of the bull case; the question is whether management's FY27 guidance on paints losses was genuine guidance or investor-relations framing.

JP|260521.view:
JPMorgan's note is the most intellectually balanced in the coverage: it acknowledges the paints beat (19% QoQ headline revenue growth, stronger than JPMe) and the on-track breakeven glide path, while explicitly flagging that the implied holdco discount remains elevated — the honest hedge that most sell-side notes gloss over.

The PT raise of ₹280 (~9%) is meaningful but moderate relative to MorganStanley's ₹3,900, reflecting JP's continued pricing of discount risk. This is the right stance. The holdco discount is structural to how Indian markets price conglomerates with large unlisted optionalities (Paints, Pivot) alongside liquid stakes in UltraTech. Until Birla Opus is unambiguously margin-positive and Pivot is demonstrably scaling, the discount persists. JP's OW at ₹3,460 is the most defensible risk-adjusted call in the group.

Kotak|260521.change: Upgraded to ADD; PT raised ₹3,000→₹3,335 (prior rating not recorded in library).
Kotak|260521.view:
Kotak's upgrade is the most actionable signal in this batch — the historically cautious construction-materials desk (sector view: Cautious) moved to ADD after Q4FY26 EBITDA beat on core divisions and narrowing paint losses. The house guided for 50%+ YoY paints revenue growth in Q4 and double-digit growth with a substantial loss reduction in FY27.

The ₹3,335 target remains the most conservative among covering houses, which is defensible: the sector-level caution and the structural holdco discount have not disappeared. This upgrade says 'Q4 execution de-risked the near-term bear case' — not that the full bull thesis is validated. As a SOTP-driven call following a clean quarter it is credible, and the upgrade is a useful signal that the stock's prior underperformance had created an asymmetric entry.

Jeff|260520.view:
Jefferies provides the most operationally detailed note in the set: VSF EBITDA doubled YoY on mix, efficiencies, and low pulp prices; Paints grew 52% YoY / 19% QoQ at ~₹14bn (beat); B2B Ecomm (Pivot) expected to turn profitable by FY27 exit; and Grasim committed ₹28.8bn into Aditya Birla Capital using surplus UltraTech dividends — a notable capital allocation data point.

I find the FY27 Pivot profitability call optimistic — B2B ecommerce/procurement in India has seen well-funded failures, and the competitive and working-capital dynamics are challenging. VSF's pulp-cost tailwind is real but cyclical; the margin profile at peak pulp will look materially different. The ₹3,600 target is reasonable on a parts-sum basis but does not fully credit the holdco discount or Pivot execution risk. Still, Jefferies' detailed operational breakdown is the most useful analytical input in the group.

MO|260211.change: PT raised ₹3,600→₹3,700 vs prior Jan-2026 note (₹3,600, Buy); Buy maintained. Inferred from Trendlyne series — no matching pdfdata entry.
MO|260211.view:
This is the stalest note in the coverage group — dated February 2026, predating the strong Q4FY26 earnings beat and the subsequent upgrades and PT raises by JP, Kotak, and Jefferies in May 2026. The headline 'strong performance; high-growth businesses in traction' is broadly consistent with subsequent quarters but the model and TP predate Q4 actuals.

MO has been a persistent Buy on Grasim across its entire visible history (all Trendlyne entries from mid-2024 onward carry Buy), which signals conviction but also means individual notes carry limited marginal information. A post-Q4FY26 update, which would incorporate the strong standalone EBITDA, paints acceleration, and Kotak's upgrade, is overdue. Treat this note as background color only until MO publishes a fresh Q4 read.

Gujarat Gas.summary:
Seven houses cover Gujarat Gas, spanning a wide range: Nomura is the lone recent bull at ₹511 (Buy, 2 Jun 2026), JPMorgan is the clear bear at ₹270 (UW), and four of the remaining five cluster around Hold — CLSA at ₹375, Jefferies at ₹415, BOB Capital at ₹406, and PL (now at Hold ₹432 after upgrading from Sell in Aug 2025). ICICI's Feb 2025 Buy at ₹560 is now stale by over a year. The stock was trading at ~₹390 at the time of the June 2026 reports, so Nomura (+31%) is the lone meaningful upside call while JPMorgan implies ~31% downside. The real debate is: how should the newly amalgamated Gujarat Energy entity — which grafts GSPL's gas transmission, GSPC's upstream/gas trading, and a power/regas business onto the original CGD franchise — be valued? Jefferies just upgraded from UW to Hold on a near-term Morbi tailwind (propane unavailability driving ceramics back to gas), raising CGD EBITDA 45% for FY27E. JPMorgan's concern centres on CGD margin compression and the power business dragging consolidated earnings (4QFY26 consolidated PAT ₹3.5bn, down 46% QoQ vs standalone ₹5.2bn). CLSA is agnostic, maintaining Hold at ₹375 — neutral on the beat but cautious on the merger complexity.

My own read: This is a fundamentally changed entity post-merger and the market hasn't fully re-rated it either way. The core CGD franchise in Gujarat is high-quality — Morbi ceramics industrial volumes are a legitimate earnings lever and Gujarat's household penetration is among the best in the CGD sector. But the GSPC/GSPL overlay is a real concern: both are government-controlled businesses with lower efficiency, commodity-price exposure (gas trading is inherently volatile), and structural power-sector headwinds. The amalgamation creates a conglomerate discount problem that the pure-play CGD multiple doesn't capture. I'd land closer to CLSA/Jefferies/BOB (₹375–₹415 range) rather than Nomura's optimistic ₹511. JPMorgan's ₹270 feels too punitive if the CGD business continues its volume recovery — but the consolidated earnings visibility is genuinely poor this early into the merger. The two things I'd watch: (1) CGD margin trajectory through FY27 as Morbi volumes normalise and the propane tailwind fades; (2) whether the gas trading/power contribution is genuinely earnings-accretive or a drag that erodes the valuation multiple.

Nomura|260602.view:
Nomura's ₹511 is the most aggressive call in the pack and implies ~31% upside from the ₹390 close. The report is titled 'Rating Remains' — it kept Buy while raising the PT materially, suggesting Nomura has taken a more bullish view on the amalgamated entity than the street consensus.

I'd discount this somewhat. Nomura is embedding assumptions that the non-CGD businesses (gas trading, upstream, power) will contribute meaningfully to earnings — assumptions that are very early-stage and unproven. The CGD fundamentals are solid, but ₹511 looks like a scenario where everything goes right with the merger. Worth tracking whether Nomura's FY27 PAT estimates prove out; if the CGD volume recovery is strong and gas trading adds accretion, the call has legs. But it's an outlier for a reason.

CLSA|260601.change: PT ₹375, HOLD — unchanged from prior report (prevTP ₹375, prevCall HOLD).
CLSA|260601.view:
CLSA is the most measured voice here. It treats the 4QFY26 result (₹5.2bn net profit, up 251% YoY, down 25% QoQ) as a 'beat on volume' but holds its view neutral. CLSA's framing of the merged entity — CGD + transmission + upstream + gas trading — is descriptive rather than enthusiastic.

Hold at ₹375 with no target change is essentially a 'wait-and-see' call on the merger. This is credible; the merged entity's earnings quality won't be clear for two or three quarters. CLSA's neutral stance is probably the most intellectually honest given the information available at the 4QFY26 first-look stage.

JP|260601.change: PT ₹270, UW — unchanged from prior report (prevTP ₹270, prevCall UW).
JP|260601.view:
JPMorgan's concern is pointed: consolidated PAT of ₹3.5bn was down 46% QoQ, with CGD margins under pressure and the power business dragging. The new amalgamated entity includes businesses JPMorgan views as structurally challenged, and they are sticking to Underweight at ₹270 — implying ~31% downside from ₹390.

This is the most intellectually contrarian call and deserves respect: JPMorgan is not just reacting to one bad quarter but questioning the structural merit of the amalgamation for Gujarat Gas shareholders. The concern about valuation compression from mixing a CGD utility multiple with a power/trading/upstream multiple is valid. That said, ₹270 may embed a scenario where the CGD volume recovery fails — the Morbi industrial recovery and propane-to-gas switch are real tailwinds. I'd watch JPMorgan's next update closely to see if they moderate.

Jeff|260601.change: PT raised ₹280→₹415; upgraded to Hold from Underperform. The prior call (Underperform) is confirmed by the report summary ('Upgrade to Hold from Underperform'); prevTP ₹280 is from pdfdata.
Jeff|260601.view:
Jefferies' upgrade is driven by a specific, near-term catalyst: propane unavailability in Morbi is pushing ceramics manufacturers back to gas, driving market share gains and margin expansion. Jefferies raised CGD EBITDA by 45% for FY27E on the back of strong Morbi volumes and introduced the gas trading business into its model post-amalgamation, arriving at ₹415 via SoTP.

This is a pragmatic upgrade — Jefferies is not suddenly bullish on the structural story, just acknowledging a real near-term tailwind. The honest read of their SoTP at ₹415 is 'only 4% upside from current levels' — so a Hold at best, not conviction. The Morbi propane-to-gas dynamic is worth watching: propane prices are cyclical, and when propane becomes available again, this tailwind reverses. Jefferies' upgrade should be read as 'less bad' rather than 'exciting'.

BOB|260601.change: PT raised ₹379→₹406; Hold maintained. Based on trendlyne: prior BOB Capital note (260121) was Hold at ₹379; current (260601) is Hold at ₹406.
BOB|260601.view:
BOB Capital's framing — 'Transitioning from CGD Utility to Energy Conglomerate' — captures the identity challenge for the stock precisely. The raise from ₹379 to ₹406 is modest and the Hold is maintained, reflecting comfort with the CGD business but uncertainty about conglomerate complexity.

BOB's ₹406 is close to Jefferies' ₹415 and broadly consistent with a fair-value range on the CGD business alone. Its note is useful context but not differentiated — it seems to acknowledge the merger without having strong conviction on the non-CGD businesses either way.

PL|250806.change: Upgraded to Hold from Sell; PT raised ₹372→₹432. Based on trendlyne: prior PL note (250521) was Sell at ₹372; current (250806) is Hold at ₹432.
PL|250806.view:
PL's upgrade from Sell to Hold in Aug 2025 reversed a downgrade from earlier in 2025 (250207 Sell ₹395, 250521 Sell ₹372). The Aug 2025 note reflects Q1FY26 results — a period before the amalgamation closed, so PL was evaluating the legacy CGD business.

This note is now dated (Aug 2025 vs Jun 2026 reports from other houses), so the PL view does not reflect the amalgamated entity. PL's current Hold stance should be treated as stale — the merger fundamentally changes the investment case and PL has not yet issued an updated view in the library.

ICICI|250208.change: Upgraded to Buy from Sell; PT raised ₹350→₹560. Based on trendlyne: prior ICICI note (240509) was Sell at ₹350; current (250208) is Buy at ₹560.
ICICI|250208.view:
ICICI's Feb 2025 Buy at ₹560 is now over 16 months old and predates the amalgamation. The thesis ('flattish Q3FY25 result; prospects look better for next 12 months') was written in the context of the pre-merger Gujarat Gas with a Q3FY25 result. The ₹560 target, already above where the stock has traded since, is clearly stale.

This call should be treated as vestigial. ICICI has not updated coverage in the library since Feb 2025. The amalgamation structurally changes the entity and any FY26/FY27 model from pre-merger data is unreliable. Disregard for current positioning — watch for a fresh ICICI note post-merger.

Gujarat Pipavav Port.summary:
Two houses covered GPPL within 24 hours of the same FY4Q26 results yet sit on opposite sides of the trade. **Kotak** upgraded to Buy (PT ₹186, raised from ₹172) citing a strong quarter, annual price hikes, and the upcoming Far East container service from July; **Jefferies** stayed at Underperform (PT ₹120, unchanged) flagging Middle East tensions as a near-term volume headwind and concession-renewal updates as 12–18 months away. The TP spread is 1.55× — ₹186 vs ₹120 — unusually wide for a single port asset. The real debate is not the quarterly beat but two structural questions: (1) whether the transshipment uplift from Middle East route disruption is durable or a temporary diversion that reverses on normalisation; and (2) whether GPPL's concession gets renewed on acceptable terms, which Jefferies treats as an unresolved overhang and Kotak largely glosses over.

My own read: GPPL has a genuine operational track record — cost discipline and blended-realisation improvement are real, and the 260bps margin expansion this quarter is not a fluke. But the competitive moat is thin relative to Mundra or JNPA, and the Maersk parentage is a double-edged sword: it provides anchor volumes but Maersk optimises its own network first. Jefferies is right to flag the concession risk as under-appreciated — a port where terminal tenure is uncertain within 12–18 months deserves a discount, not a premium re-rating. The new Far East service is a genuine catalyst but I would wait to see volume ramp before crediting it in the multiple. Kotak's ₹186 implies both the service launch and concession clarity materialising — two conditions, not one. I lean closer to Jefferies' structural caution, though the near-term earnings momentum makes an outright short uncomfortable. A ₹140–155 range looks more defensible than either extreme.

Kotak|260601.change: PT raised ₹172→₹186; report title states upgrade to BUY (prior call not captured in pdfdata — exact prior rating cannot be confirmed from that source alone).
Kotak|260601.view:
Kotak's upgrade is well-timed to a beat quarter and a constructive near-term setup. The 7–8% EBITDA estimate raise is grounded in realisation improvement and cost discipline, both of which are visible in the results. The thesis hinges on the July Far East service as the next re-rating catalyst — reasonable, but binary: if volumes diversify away from Middle East exposure ₹186 is achievable; if the service under-ramps or Middle East tensions ease (reducing transshipment), the upgrade unwinds quickly.

What I'd push back on: Kotak appears to treat part of the transshipment uplift as structural, but transshipment is notoriously fickle and follows the cheapest route. The concession overhang gets minimal attention in this note, which is the one risk Jefferies is explicitly pricing. Key watch-points are July–September container volume trends and any concession announcement — those two data points will confirm or challenge whether this upgrade was premature.

Jeff|260531.view:
Jefferies' bear case rests on two legs: near-term volume uncertainty from Middle East tensions and the 12–18 month horizon on concession updates. That the quarter came in 13% above JEFe yet Jefferies held its target and rating signals the valuation discount is deliberate — they are not ignoring the beat, they are discounting the terminal value.

This is probably the more rigorous structural view of the two. The concession point is one the market tends to dismiss until it suddenly cannot. At ₹120, Jefferies prices in minimal credit for concession extension beyond current terms — arguably harsh given Maersk's strategic interest in maintaining the port's viability, but it is the correct question to keep asking. I give this note high credibility on the structural risk, even if the near-term earnings momentum makes the outright Underperform a difficult hold in a rising market. The honest use of this note is as a checklist of what needs to be resolved before GPPL deserves a re-rating: concession terms and Far East service ramp.

Hindalco.summary:
Five houses are outright bullish (**CLSA** OP ₹1,240, **JPMorgan** OW ₹1,180, **Emkay** Buy ₹1,100, **MO** Buy ₹1,110, **BOB** Buy ₹1,050), two are neutral/Hold (**Jeff** ₹1,075, **Axis** ₹1,050), and one is a lone bear (**Kotak** Reduce ₹1,100). Target prices cluster ₹1,050–₹1,110 for the median camp with CLSA a clear outlier at ₹1,240. Every house has raised its PT since its prior note (Jefferies most dramatically: ₹890→₹1,075), driven by the 4QFY26 results beat and elevated LME. The real split is not on the India business — everyone acknowledges the aluminum/copper EBITDA beat — but on **Novelis**: whether multiple fire incidents (including Oswego) are a temporary operational disruption or a signal of deeper execution risk, and whether the Bay Minett capex overrun makes the IRR case deteriorate. Axis's February downgrade is now three months stale and predates the strong 4Q results; it is the weakest read in the current set.

My own read: Hindalco's India business is genuinely high quality — captive coal, sulfuric acid byproduct kicker from the copper smelter, and a long expansion runway in the Aditya aluminium smelter. The LME tailwind is real and, in a world of US tariff friction on Chinese metals, could have staying power. But **Novelis is the binary**. Bay Minett (new greenfield in Canada) is a ₹15,000+ Cr capex project whose IRR assumptions were built on lower aluminium costs and a smoother ramp; every capex revision and delay compresses the return. Oswego's fire-related disruption is theoretically recoverable, but the recurrence of safety incidents (two in quick succession per Jeff's note) raises operational culture questions that a single restart won't answer. Net debt/EBITDA at 1.83x is manageable now but will climb through peak capex FY27-28. I'd be more comfortable with Hindalco as a tactical trade on LME momentum than a long-duration hold at current valuations. The **two things to watch**: Oswego hot-mill restart confirmation in June 2026, and the next Bay Minett capex disclosure.

CLSA|260524.view:
CLSA's 20% PT raise is the most aggressive in the set and reflects a near-full pass-through of the LME spot uplift (+$470/t vs Q4) into earnings — they are essentially running the India business at current spot and ignoring mean-reversion risk. The 4QFY26 India EBITDA beat of 12% validates the near-term thesis, and CLSA's framing of "strong tailwinds" until expansion project commissioning is fair.

The problem is the ₹1,240 target leaves almost no margin of safety if LME corrects or Novelis drags longer than expected. CLSA seems to be treating Novelis as a rounding error, which feels aggressive. This is the call you want to own if commodities stay elevated and Oswego restarts cleanly; it is also the first one to revisit if either condition breaks.

JP|260524.view:
The near-flat PT revision (+₹5 on a ₹1,175 base) despite a 13% EBITDA beat is telling — JPMorgan is being disciplined, not euphoric. Their dissection is the most granular: they flag that the copper EBITDA surprise was largely sulfuric acid realizations (₹9bn vs JPMe ₹6.1bn), a byproduct-driven beat that may not repeat at the same magnitude. The net debt/EBITDA creep to 1.83x from 1.73x was also caught explicitly.

JP's OW is the most credible bull call in the set because it isn't stretching the target. Their implicit message is that the stock is fairly priced at current levels with upside optionality from Novelis normalization. The moderate conviction is appropriate.

Kotak|260524.view:
Kotak is the lone bear and the most intellectually honest: they acknowledged the EBITDA beat across divisions, raised their PT by 10%, but kept Reduce. The thesis is purely valuation — they are not disputing the operational improvement, they are arguing the market has already priced it in. Their specific insight on coal mine cost benefit only accruing from FY2028 is underappreciated: bulls are modelling margin expansion now, but the structural cost advantage is back-end loaded.

The Novelis Oswego normalization in 2HFY27 is also a key assumption for the bull camp. Kotak's scepticism there is the useful counterweight. A Reduce at ₹1,100 PT on a ₹1,100 stock implies almost zero upside and meaningful downside from Novelis or LME risk — that's a defensible positioning, even if the absolute bear case is limited.

Jeff|260522.view:
Jefferies made the biggest absolute PT revision in the set (up 21%) while keeping Hold — a classic calibration exercise after being caught low. The EPS upgrades of 11-14% for FY27-28 on higher aluminium prices are model mechanics, not a change in structural view. What stands out in Jeff's note is the explicit flagging of "multiple fire incidents" clouding Novelis' operational outlook — they are the only house to emphasise the safety/recurrence angle rather than just the Oswego financial drag.

Jeff's Hold at 3% downside to their own PT is essentially a flat call. The more useful takeaway is that their 11-14% EPS upgrade still lands them at Hold, implying the stock has already rerated to price in that improvement. That is the same message as Kotak but with less conviction in the bear direction. I find Jeff's Novelis safety concern the most underweighted point across the coverage.
